rv.q: If, however, you like this sort of thing, then Richard Fitch's gleefully scene-chewing production is worth seeing for a couple of sensational performances.
It’s homage rather than satire, with the bite of the alco- consistently outdone by the sweetness of the -pop.
It's fun and flimsy, this revival, but in the end it just doesn't hold together and, at times, it is positively laboured.

Richard Fitch’s production hits all the show’s campy bases, but the slapstick is fumbled, and the murderous gore is so tame that none of the audience, even its child star, will need to sleep with the night light on afterwards.
Instead, it’s a full flow of really bland songs and cheap, tasteless gags which a mostly admirable cast can’t redeem.
Director Richard Fitch has created an outstanding comic company.
The show may be ridiculous, and more than a little shonky, but the performances are sublime and make the evening a blast of comic Broadway excess.
I just wish he and the exceptionally gifted company had a better show to work with.
It is musically mundane but it is also rude and catty and I'm afraid I laughed quite a lot.

cn.t: This campy 1992 off-Broadway parody of showbiz ambition receives mixed reviews, with critics finding it funny but uneven. While praised for over-the-top performances and theatrical in-jokes, many note the material feels dated and overstuffed.
